To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

incorporating both human control and feedback in a single system can improve task performance and that varying human feedback parameters can impact agent performance in interactive machine learning tasks.

(i) incorporating human feedback in addition to control signals can improve performance in interactive machine learning systems; (ii) the probability of giving human feedback and the likelihood of the feedback being correct can impact performance; and (iii) temporal smearing can be used to improve the effectiveness of human feedback.

the temporal decay of human feedback, the probability of giving human feedback, and the probability that the human feedback is 'correct' are important factors for learning algorithms to act in human-machine interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a framework for the design and implementation of human-machine systems in which the human and the machine learn together, and in which the human is an active partner in the learning process.
the development of an RL-based interactive robotic system that models the human user through interaction and multisensory perception.
the development of a reinforcement learning (RL) agent that can model human reward and learn how to interact with human users through multi-sensory perception and control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human-machine interaction is a very complex domain that requires further investigation.
human feedback and human control signals can be used to complement each other in a system which models human reward.
the human feedback is an essential part of the learning process and the more accurate the feedback is, the faster and more accurate the agent learns the task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how human control and feedback can complement each other in interactive machine learning.
human feedback and human control can complement each other to achieve better performance.
we have developed a novel approach to interactive reinforcement learning, which allows us to learn from human feedback, and to model the human reward function.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the human feedback signal is a valuable source of information for an agent to learn about its environment, and that incorporating this signal can improve the performance of interactive robotic systems.
the human feedback can significantly improve performance of RL agents.
incorporating human feedback in a reinforcement learning system can improve task performance and that the way the human feedback is processed is crucial to the success of the task.
